title: Granular approval and immutable audit for automated batching/cache applies
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Design and implement a secure, auditable change-management flow for automatic batching and KV-cache configuration changes. The goal is to allow the Optimize/autotune subsystem to propose and apply cost-saving batching/cache suggestions while enforcing separation-of-duties, tamper-evident audit trails, and reversible, safe rollbacks. This ticket covers authorization (RBAC + SCIM mapping), signed change bundles, an immutable append-only audit store, policy checks (Rego/OPA), canary rollout choreography, and forensic export for compliance reviews.

Motivation:
- Automated cost changes reduce unit economics but introduce operational and compliance risk if misapplied.
- We need technical controls to satisfy enterprise auditors: approval records, unforgeable evidence of who approved/applied, and reliable rollback triggers.

Scope (in-scope):
- Authorization model: fine-grained roles (Autotune-Operator, Autotune-Reviewer, Autotune-Escalator) mapped to Okta/SCIM groups.
- Signed change bundles: autotune proposals packaged, hashed, and signed with customer/cluster KMS key or Redwood HSM for hosted clusters.
- Immutable audit store: append-only log (WORM semantics) with export hooks to SIEM/S3 and retention policies.
- Policy evaluation: OPA/Rego policy set that gates risky changes (e.g., >20% batch increase, KV eviction risk, changes for PII-handling pools).
- Rollout orchestration: staged canaries (1% -> 10% -> 100%) with automated metric checks and a signed commit once stabilized.
- Automatic rollback: triggers for cost/latency/quality regressions with audit note and optional human escalation.

Out-of-scope: detailed UI work for Console (separate PM/design ticket), private deployment packaging (minor integration items to follow).
acceptance_criteria:
AC-1: Every autotune 'apply' produces a signed change bundle (bundle ID attached to telemetry/traces) stored in the immutable audit store.
AC-2: RBAC enforced: only members of Autotune-Operator can execute canary applies; only Autotune-Reviewer can approve full rollouts; separation-of-duties prevents same user approving and applying a full rollout.
AC-3: OPA policies block changes violating predefined risk thresholds; blocked proposals are recorded with policy decision log.
AC-4: Canary stages run automatically and evaluate at least: median latency delta, p50/p95 token rate, and eval-set quality regression. If any metric breaches thresholds, the system auto-rolls back within the defined window and records reason.
AC-5: Audit store exports to SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) and supports forensic export to S3 with integrity proofs (bundle hash + KMS signature).
AC-6: Playbook for auditors and incident responders (steps to validate signatures, verify approvals, reconstruct rollout traces) committed to Confluence and linked from the ticket.
design_notes:
Key design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use signed change bundles instead of only logging to ensure non-repudiation and tamper-evidence. Bundles include: proposal metadata, diff of runtime config, proposed canary plan, policy decision snapshot, signer identity.
- Signatures: hosted clusters use Redwood HSM signing keys; Dedicated/Private deployments may provision customer KMS keys. We will implement an abstraction layer so the same bundle format works for both.
- Immutable store: implement on top of existing events DB with append-only mode + daily Merkle snapshot persisted to S3. This avoids building a separate blockchain-like system while providing verifiable integrity.
- Policy engine: evaluate proposals pre-apply using OPA (Rego). Policy decision logs are stored as part of the bundle.
- RBAC model: map roles to SCIM groups from Okta/Google workspace; support short-lived delegation tokens for operator runbooks.
- Rollback window: default 30 minutes post-rollout; configurable per proposal. Fast rollback uses precomputed rollback manifest included in bundle to ensure idempotent revert.
- Cost vs. speed trade-off: canary cadence (1%/10%/100%) balances risk and time-to-value; we will allow admins to configure more conservative defaults for high-risk customers.

Open questions:
- For Dedicated customers, who owns signing keys by default? (Customer KMS recommended but we need onboarding flow.)
- Retention window for audit store by default (90 days vs. 1 year) pending compliance feedback.
- How to surface approvals/denials within Console without exposing sensitive KMS metadata?
rollout_plan:
Phased rollout:
Phase 1 (internal): feature-flag behind 'autotune-signed-apply' for platform SRE and infra devs. End-to-end tests with local KMS and Redwood HSM mock.
Phase 2 (pilot customers): enable for 3 low-risk Dedicated customers + 5 hosted customers opted-in; collect feedback and telemetry.
Phase 3 (general availability): enable for all customers with default conservative thresholds; Console UI and PM UX follow-on.
Fail-safe: all auto-applies create a 'safety tombstone' that can be used by SRE to immediately freeze autotune applies for a customer/region.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Metrics to track: signed_bundle_count, apply_success_rate, rollback_rate, policy_block_rate, time_to_rollback, approval_latency.
Alerts: P1 if rollback_rate > 2% across customers in 1h with correlated latency regression; P0 if any apply results in SLO breach for >5% of traffic.
Dashboards: per-customer apply history with bundle IDs linked to traces and PRs.
Forensics: automated daily job verifies Merkle snapshots and alerts on mismatch.

2025-10-14 Ravi Patel (Security): Reviewed signature model. Request: include certificate chain and signer role in bundle metadata. Also require 'emergency-apply' audit flow with detailed justification logs.
2025-10-22 Rafael Ortega: Implemented prototype for bundle format and OPA policy hooks. Created branch runtime/autotune-signed-bundles. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5421

2025-11-02 QA: Integration smoke tests for canary orchestration passing in staging. Found edge case where policy evaluation was non-deterministic for timestamped policies; fixed policy runtime to normalize timestamps.
2025-11-15 Compliance: Confirmed export format meets auditor needs for 'who/when/what' with signature proofs. Requested retention default change to 365d for enterprise customers.
